Topic 3.5: Jesus raises a Widow’s Son

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Jesus raises a Widow’s Son. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What do you learn from the miracle of raising the widow’s son?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. retell the story of raising the widow’s son
2. recognise God’s power over life and death
3. apply lessons learnt by showing compassion to others
4. pray to God when faced with challenges

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: JESUS RAISES A WIDOW’S SON
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Jesus raises a Widow’s Son helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: JESUS RAISES A WIDOW’S SON
Study Jesus raises a Widow’s Son like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Retell the story of raising the widow’s son

What this means
In this part you learn to retell the story of raising the widow’s son. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: retell the story of raising the widow’s son.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Jesus raises a Widow’s Son” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can retell the story of raising the widow’s son. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Recognise God’s power over life and death

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise God’s power over life and death. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise God’s power over life and death.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Jesus raises a Widow’s Son in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise God’s power over life and death. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Apply lessons learnt by showing compassion to others

What this means
In this part you learn to apply lessons learnt by showing compassion to others. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply lessons learnt by showing compassion to others.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply lessons learnt by showing compassion to others. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Pray to God when faced with challenges

What this means
In this part you learn to pray to God when faced with challenges. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: pray to God when faced with challenges.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Jesus raises a Widow’s Son” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can pray to God when faced with challenges. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Jesus raises a Widow’s Son is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Jesus raises a Widow’s Son” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: retell the story of raising the widow’s son)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Jesus raises a Widow’s Son in your own words. (skill: recognise God’s power over life and death)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: apply lessons learnt by showing compassion to others)

Example 4: Show how “Jesus raises a Widow’s Son” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: pray to God when faced with challenges)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Jesus raises a Widow’s Son to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: retell the story of raising the widow’s son.
3. Practise this skill: recognise God’s power over life and death.
4. Practise this skill: apply lessons learnt by showing compassion to others.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Jesus raises a Widow’s Son from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Jesus raises a Widow’s Son: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Jesus raises a Widow’s Son?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What do you learn from the miracle of raising the widow’s son?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Jesus raises a Widow’s Son means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: retell the story of raising the widow’s son.
5. Be able to: recognise God’s power over life and death.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
